epics.title: Backend Application Context Initialization Repair
epics.jtbd: When an operator starts the system, I want the application context to load successfully, so that the backend can execute standard workflows.
requirements: R1: Fix backend environment dependencies or database properties to allow successful ApplicationContext startup.
R2: Ensure test suite (mvn test) runs without IllegalStateException application context failures.
R3: Note: Remaining links in the epidemiological core loop (e.g. searching, reporting) are structurally handled by other epics, this epic focuses strictly on application startup viability.

slices.title: Backend Context Initialization Fix
slices.jtbd: When implementing the context fix for this epic, I want to resolve property or dependency mismatches, so that the Spring boot application starts without errors.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the backend environment, When starting the application, Then no IllegalStateException is thrown.
Given the test suite, When running tests, Then the application context loads successfully.

slices.title: Backend Context Initialization QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify that the backend loads cleanly across test and runtime profiles, so that integration is robust.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the build pipeline, When executing tests, Then zero tests fail due to context load errors.
Given a fresh deployment, When starting the service, Then the health check reports healthy.

epics.title: Frontend to Backend Real API Connection
epics.jtbd: When an end customer interacts with the frontend, I want the application to communicate with the real backend API, so that actions result in genuine confirmations rather than static mock answers.
requirements: R1: Remove static mock responses from serve.mjs.
R2: Establish real HTTP connections between frontend UI components and actual backend controllers.
R3: Provide visible feedback and real confirmations based on genuine backend responses.
R4: Ensure that what the user typed survives if a backend connection fails or validation rejects the input.
R5: Note: Known chains like PDF generation and search are verified in this epic strictly through establishing the real API connection capability rather than re-implementing them.

slices.title: Frontend API Integration Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing API integration for this epic, I want to replace mock fetching with actual backend calls, so that the UI reflects real system state.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a UI action, When triggered, Then a real API request is dispatched to the backend.
Given a failed backend request, When the response returns an error, Then the user's input survives in the form.
Given a backend operation, When processing, Then visible feedback is displayed to the user.
Given any UI layout, When rendered, Then it passes WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard operability, visible focus, and contrast checks.

slices.title: Frontend API Integration QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to test the full E2E journey, so that mock usage is proven eradicated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the E2E test suite, When completing user journeys, Then all assertions pass using the real database and backend.
Given network failure simulation, When submitting a form, Then the input is preserved and error feedback is visible.

epics.title: Repair API Authentication Invariants
epics.jtbd: When an authorized client makes a valid request, I want the API to accept it with 200/201, so that the core product features (search, document listing, report generation) are usable.
requirements: R1: Fix SecurityConfig rules to permit authorized users access to employee dossier and protocols endpoints.
R2: Ensure previously failing tests expecting 200/201 no longer receive 401 Unauthorized.
R3: Note: The core epidemiological capabilities like search and pdf generation are technically complete in backend, this strictly unblocks the authorization chain required to use them.

slices.title: Security Configuration Fixes
slices.jtbd: When implementing security fixes for this epic, I want to map roles accurately to endpoint permissions, so that legitimate traffic is authorized.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid user session, When accessing dossier and protocol endpoints, Then access is granted (HTTP 200/201).
Given an invalid or missing token, When accessing the same endpoints, Then the request is rejected with 401.

slices.title: Authentication Invariant QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify role-based access across all endpoints, so that the API meets its authorization contract.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the test suite, When executed on main, Then the 22 failing tests regarding 401 errors now pass.
Given different authorized roles, When tested against protected routes, Then correct HTTP statuses are returned.

epics.title: Enactive Perception and Genuine UI Load States
epics.jtbd: When an end customer interacts with the frontend, I want actions to reflect genuine internal dynamic feedback without artificial disconnects, so that the enactive perception space is maintained.
requirements: R1: Integrate the Impressum/Imprint into the visual layout naturally instead of using a blocking native browser alert().
R2: Ensure the Impressum/Imprint is reachable from every page to satisfy regulatory constraints.
R3: Tie the dossier generation loading state to actual backend lifecycle events rather than using hardcoded setTimeout.
R4: Note: Generative and processing chains depend on this UI state refinement to provide proper real-time loading feedback rather than simulating processing times.

slices.title: UI Dynamic State Refactoring
slices.jtbd: When implementing UI updates for this epic, I want to replace artificial timeouts and alerts with genuine state transitions, so that the UI faithfully represents backend activity.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the application layout, When the user clicks the Imprint, Then it renders smoothly within the DOM without an alert().
Given a dossier generation process, When it begins, Then the loading spinner persists exactly as long as the backend request takes.
Given the application footer, When navigating any route, Then the Imprint link remains visible and functional.
Given any UI layout, When rendered, Then it passes WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard operability, visible focus, and contrast checks.

slices.title: UI Dynamic State QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to assert that UI states map directly to network events, so that artificial disconnects are proven removed.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given E2E tests, When triggering the Imprint, Then no unexpected browser alerts are intercepted.
Given simulated network latency, When generating a dossier, Then the UI loading state duration exactly matches the network delay.

epics.title: Empirical Dossier Analytics Reporting
epics.jtbd: When a researcher queries employee dossier analytics, I want to receive strictly empirical data, so that I am not misled by calculated guesswork presented as statistical certainty.
requirements: R1: Remove synthetic margin of error calculations (lowerBound, upperBound) utilizing hardcoded 1.96 constants and Math.sqrt.
R2: Remove silent 0.0 fallbacks for NaN values in the EmployeeDossierAnalyticsController.
R3: Report only empirical facts (raw counts and strict ratios) or compute statistically sound intervals tied to actual observations.
R4: Note: The broader analytical dossier chain is established; this epic focuses strictly on removing hallucinated variance numbers from its presentation.

slices.title: Analytics Logic Refactoring
slices.jtbd: When implementing analytics changes for this epic, I want to strip unfounded synthetic bounds, so that the endpoint delivers only observable facts.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an analytics payload, When calculated, Then it only includes raw counts and strict ratios without synthetic lowerBound/upperBound fields.
Given an edge case where a ratio denominator is zero, When processing, Then it correctly returns null or an explicit error instead of silently falling back to 0.0.

slices.title: Analytics Reporting QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify the absence of synthetic data, so that empirical integrity is mathematically proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API integration tests, When asserting the analytics response, Then no synthetic margin fields exist in the JSON payload.
Given sparse or empty test data, When requesting analytics, Then the response correctly reflects nulls/errors rather than 0.0 approximations.

epics.title: Monotonic Causal Tracking for Telemetry
epics.jtbd: When the system generates telemetry, I want processing durations to be measured using monotonic causal tokens, so that accurate incident reconstruction is immune to transient local clock variances.
requirements: R1: Replace System.currentTimeMillis() subtraction for processing time in EmployeeDossierAnalyticsController with monotonically increasing causal tokens or explicit causal bounds.
R2: Note: The ingestion and rendering links for telemetry are built; this targets only causal consistency of the timing value emitted.

slices.title: Telemetry Causal Mechanism Implementation
slices.jtbd: When implementing telemetry timing for this epic, I want to adopt monotonic tokens (e.g. nanoTime or distributed traces), so that durations are strictly causally bounded.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a dossier processing workflow, When tracking duration, Then monotonic sources or causal tokens are used instead of currentTimeMillis.
Given a thread context switch, When completing processing, Then the duration cannot mathematically be negative.

slices.title: Telemetry Causal Tracking QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to verify telemetry durations under concurrent load, so that timing stability is proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given concurrent processing tests, When telemetry events are emitted, Then all measured durations strictly uphold happens-before relationships.
Given a simulated system clock shift during processing, When asserting the tracked duration, Then it remains accurate and unaffected.

epics.title: Knowledge-First Recovery Path Security
epics.jtbd: When a user accesses recovery endpoints, I want the system to enforce strict knowledge-grade checks, so that state transitions cannot be triggered by unverified claims.
requirements: R1: Remove the global permitAll bypass for /api/v1/recovery/** in SecurityConfig.
R2: Enforce explicit knowledge-grade checks (e.g., secure tokens or prior authenticated states) for all sensitive recovery state transitions.
R3: Note: The base self-service recovery chain exists, this epic strictly applies authentication rigor to its execution endpoint.

slices.title: Recovery Endpoint Hardening
slices.jtbd: When implementing access control for this epic, I want to remove unauthenticated recovery bypasses, so that the knowledge boundary is secure.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an unauthenticated request to /api/v1/recovery/**, When received, Then it is strictly rejected with a 401/403.
Given a request providing a valid, securely issued recovery token, When received, Then the recovery action is permitted.

slices.title: Recovery Security QA
slices.jtbd: When implementing QA for this epic, I want to attempt unverified recovery access, so that the strict knowledge boundary is proven.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the integration test suite, When tests attempt to hit recovery endpoints without authentication, Then they consistently receive forbidden/unauthorized responses.
Given a valid authenticated recovery state, When tested, Then the endpoint successfully processes the request.

epics.title: Semantic Truth in Database Integration Testing
epics.jtbd: When a developer relies on integration tests, I want the tests to assert truth against the real system components, so that success implies actual system functionality rather than modeled compliance.
requirements: R1: Remove @MockBean annotations for core domain services (like UserRepository and TelemetryService) from integration tests (e.g., EmployeeDossierControllerTest).
R2: Introduce real database integration via Testcontainers to ensure tests assert against the actual system implementation.
R3: Note: All epidemiological verification chains fundamentally rely on these tests providing empirical truth over mock states.

slices.title: Testcontainers Integration Setup
slices.jtbd: When implementing test infrastructure for this epic, I want to provision real database instances using Testcontainers, so that mock components can be retired.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the integration test suite, When initialized, Then a Testcontainers-managed database spins up automatically.
Given the test execution environment, When tests complete, Then the containerized database shuts down correctly.

slices.title: Mock Removal and Authentic Assertion Refactoring
slices.jtbd: When implementing test refactoring for this epic, I want to remove mocked bounds and test against real data, so that tests establish semantic truth.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given EmployeeDossierControllerTest, When reviewing the code, Then @MockBean is entirely absent for database and telemetry services.
Given the integration test suite, When run against Testcontainers, Then all assertions pass based on actual database state modifications.
